relevance_note: Case report of one man with adult-onset Alexander disease and a GFAP variant: 'The genetic analysis finally showed a known heterozygous mutation in exon 4 (c.772C.T; p.Arg258Cys) of the GFAP gene.'
method_note: Single case report read in full by hand; output assembled with a short Python script from hand-chosen values and spans. Labels: the proband is called only 'the index patient'/'our patient' (role words), so rule 5 'patient'. Relatives in the text and Figure 1 legend: sister (MS), brother (ALS, died at 57), and 'parents' without individual sex, labelled 'parent of patient' and 'parent of patient 2'; they are in scope as relatives described as affected (by other diagnoses/gait disturbance); their genotypes are stated as unknown, so no variant rows. Discussion: 'The p.Arg258Cys mutation has been described in 2 other patients, 8,9' with one (ref 8) having AOAD with prominent autonomic dysfunction; included as 'ref 8 patient' and 'ref 9 patient' because the variant is an individual-level fact; assigning the second patient to ref 9 is an inference from the citation '8,9'. Their variant rows give the gene from the paper's own GFAP statement about p.Arg258Cys. The PDF conversion renders '>' as '.': the cDNA is printed 'c.772C.T' and the parents' onset 'AAO .60 years' (recorded as printed; no ISO value). The sentence 'Motor evoked potentials, nerve conduction studies, and biochemical testing of serum, CSF, and ... gastroscopy (exclusion of Whipple disease) were normal.' is split by the Figure 2 legend; quoted as two spans, not joined. Under D-27, normal investigations recorded as excluded abnormalities named as the paper does (abnormal FP-CIT-SPECT, MEP, nerve conduction, serum/CSF biochemistry, gastroscopy, cerebral glucose metabolism); these exclude nothing more specific. 'normal memory' excludes memory impairment only; the broader checklist item cognitive decline is left not reported. 'upper motor neuron signs' mapped to checklist 'spasticity or pyramidal signs' as observed. T2 signal increase involves brainstem/cerebellar tracts (medial longitudinal fascicles, spinocerebellar tracts, superior cerebellar peduncles), not stated cerebral white matter, so 'cerebral white matter abnormality' left not reported. Age at diagnosis not stated as an age (only '10-year disease history before the diagnosis'), left not reported. No contradictions found.
